title: Quasi-compact selection inside a relatively dense smooth open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $p:X\to S$ be smooth [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $U_s$ is topologically dense in $X_s$ for every $s\in S$, where $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $U_s=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field]. There is a quasi-compact open subscheme $W\subseteq U$ such that $W_s$ is dense in $X_s$ for every $s\in S$. Neither $S$ nor $U$ is assumed quasi-compact; empty schemes and empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: BLR 2.5, Lemma 3, printed pp.56-57, PDF pp.62-63; local copy WANTED; primary scan at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf

proof.text: If $X$ is empty take $W=\varnothing$. Otherwise apply [sbc-lem-slicing] to $p$. Write its charts as $e_i:D_i\to X$, $f_i:D_i\to T_i$, $a_i:T_i\to S$, with $p e_i=a_i f_i$. Both $D_i,T_i$ are affine, $e_i,a_i$ are etale, and $f_i$ is smooth with a section and geometrically connected nonempty fibres. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] the sets $e_i(D_i)$ are open. They cover $X$, so quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover; retain just these indices. This finite family is still an etale covering of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0EY4, lemma-cover-smooth-by-special; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT; compactness applied to the images

proof.text: Put $E_i=e_i^{-1}(U)$. Fix $t\in T_i$, set $s=a_i(t)$, and put $F_{i,t}=D_i\times_{T_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. By [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality], applied to $f_i$ with the identity field extension, $F_{i,t}$ is nonempty and integral. Base change $e_i$ to $s$; the resulting map $e_{i,s}:D_i\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to X_s$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], the point of $(T_i)_s$ corresponding to $t$ is an open subscheme isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. Its inverse image in $(D_i)_s$ is exactly $F_{i,t}$ by the fibre-product identities. Thus $F_{i,t}$ is an open subscheme of $(D_i)_s$, and the restriction $F_{i,t}\to X_s$ is an open map by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. For every nonempty open $H\subset F_{i,t}$ its image in $X_s$ is nonempty open and meets $U_s$. Consequently $H$ meets $E_i\times_{T_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. This proves that this latter open is dense and nonempty in $F_{i,t}$; in particular $f_i(E_i)=T_i$.

source.place: Tags 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), 03WT (lemma-etale-open); varieties.tex Tag 056T and more-morphisms.tex Tag 057J

proof.text: Cover $E_i$ by affine opens $A_{i,\alpha}$ of $D_i$ contained in $E_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Smoothness of $f_i$ gives flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so $f_i$ is an open map by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Hence the $f_i(A_{i,\alpha})$ form an open cover of $T_i$, by $f_i(E_i)=T_i$. The affine scheme $T_i$ is quasi-compact by clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. Select finitely many $A_{i,\alpha}$ whose images cover $T_i$, and denote their union by $B_i$. For every $t$, the open $(B_i)_t$ in $F_{i,t}$ is nonempty. It is dense: in an irreducible space two nonempty opens intersect, so every nonempty open of the integral $F_{i,t}$ meets $(B_i)_t$.

source.place: Tag 01UA, lemma-fppf-open; schemes.tex Tag 01IT; algebra.tex Tag 00E8; finite selection after smooth slicing

proof.text: Let $W=\bigcup_{i,\alpha}e_i(A_{i,\alpha})$, using only the finitely selected indices of both kinds. Each image is open in $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], and is contained in $U$ by the choice of $A_{i,\alpha}$. Each $A_{i,\alpha}$ is quasi-compact by clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], and its image is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact]. A finite union of these images is quasi-compact: restrict an open cover of their union to each image, choose its finite subcover, and take the union of these finitely many finite selections. Give $W$ its open subscheme structure. The map $B_i\to X$ factors through $W$: its image lies in $W$, and restricting the structure-sheaf map to this open gives the factorization. Thus its fibre map factors through $W_s$ for every $s$.

source.place: Tag 04Z9, lemma-image-quasi-compact; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT; finite-union open-cover argument

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and a nonempty open $H\subseteq X_s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] the retained $e_{i,s}:(D_i)_s\to X_s$ are jointly surjective. Choose $y\in e_{i,s}^{-1}(H)$ for one $i$, and let $t$ be its image in $(T_i)_s$, regarded as a point of $T_i$ over $s$. The open fibre identification of step 2 makes $e_{i,s}^{-1}(H)\cap F_{i,t}$ a nonempty open of $F_{i,t}$. By step 3 this meets $(B_i)_t$. Its image is a point of $H\cap W_s$, using the factorization of step 4. Therefore every nonempty open of $X_s$ meets $W_s$, exactly the asserted density. If $X_s$ is empty there is no such $H$ and the condition is automatic. No compactness of $S$ or $U$, nor separatedness of $X$, has been used.

Step 1: the slicing chart images are open (étale), so a finite subcover exists because X is quasi-compact. Step 2: the section makes every chart fibre nonempty, so lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality with K=κ(t) gives integral F_{i,t}. 02GL(2) makes F_{i,t} open in (D_i)_s, and since e_{i,s} is an open map, E_i∩F_{i,t} is dense and nonempty. Step 4: W is a finite union of quasi-compact open images inside U. Step 5: the covering base-changed to X_s is jointly surjective, and density follows.
